question: For a positive real number $\alpha$, let $S_\alpha$ denote the set of points $(x,y)$ satisfying $|x|^\alpha+|y|^\alpha=1$. A positive number $\alpha$ is said to be good if the points in $S_\alpha$ that are closest to the origin lie only on the coordinate axes. Then

options.A: all $\alpha$ in $(0,1)$ are good and others are not good.
options.B: all $\alpha$ in $(1,2)$ are good and others are not good.
options.C: all $\alpha>2$ are good and others are not good.
options.D: all $\alpha>1$ are good and others are not good.
